name: quote
description: A pulled quotation, centered, with attribution.
purpose: Use to land a phrase verbatim — customer voice, expert claim, mission statement. Keep under ~25 words. The quote IS the slide; the attribution is the supporting credit. `bare` drops the card, border, and quotation-mark glyphs for a plain, display-scale statement — a hook or cold-open line, not a sourced quotation.

whenToUse.title: Verbatim language matters
whenToUse.body: When the audience needs to hear the words exactly as they were said — customer feedback, expert claim, regulatory text, mission statement. Paraphrasing would lose the impact.

whenToUse.title: One breath of reading
whenToUse.body: Keep the quotation under ~25 words. The audience reads silently in one breath; longer than that and they're scanning, not feeling the words.

whenToUse.title: Attribution earns the quote
whenToUse.body: Anonymous quotes feel weak. Attribute the speaker, their role, and the context ("Head of Product, Pilot Team 3" beats just "a customer"). The attribution is the credibility.

antiPatterns.title: Paragraph-length quotes
antiPatterns.body: If the quote runs past 25 words, the slide is reading like a wall of text. Trim aggressively or use `split-panel pullquote` (gives the quote half the slide alongside spelled-out implications).

antiPatterns.title: Multiple quotes per slide
antiPatterns.body: Two quotes on one canvas dilute both. The whole point is that one quote earns the whole slide. For a montage of customer voices, use successive quote slides.

antiPatterns.title: Decorative quotes
antiPatterns.body: If the quote could be paraphrased without losing anything, the slide doesn't need to be a quote slide. Move the idea into `content` and skip the chrome.

related.name: split-panel
related.when: the quote needs implications spelled out alongside it

related.name: content
related.when: the language is paraphrasable — let prose carry it

related.name: big-number
related.when: the most memorable thing is a metric, not a phrase

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing the attribution as a second line inside the blockquote (`> quote text` then `> — Person`) instead of a separate paragraph after it.
commonMistakes.fix: The attribution slot is the paragraph AFTER the blockquote, not inside it — written inside, it inherits the blockquote's large italic quotation styling instead of the smaller attribution treatment.

commonMistakes.mistake: Splitting the quotation across two paragraphs inside the blockquote.
commonMistakes.fix: The blockquote's opening/closing smart-quote glyphs decorate the blockquote as a whole, once — two paragraphs inside it both render at full quotation size with no visual distinction, instead of the single continuous quotation the layout expects.

bare.label: bare
bare.summary: No card, no quotation marks — a plain display-scale line.
